title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of employers' organizations

description.narrative: Employers’ and business membership organizations (EBMOs) in Zimbabwe operate in a challenging and evolving economic and labour market context, characterized by high informality, macroeconomic instability, and a rapidly changing world of work. These conditions have made it difficult for EBMOs to maintain strong, representative, and financially sustainable structures, particularly in ensuring effective outreach to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and emerging sectors. In addition, capacity gaps in research, policy analysis, and negotiation skills can limit their ability to articulate a coherent and evidence-based voice of business, engage effectively in social dialogue, and participate meaningfully in collective bargaining and national policy processes. The ILO supports efforts to strengthen the institutional capacity of EBMOs to become more independent, representative, and responsive to the needs of their members. This includes enhancing their ability to expand membership, improve service delivery, and strengthen internal governance systems, while building technical competencies for effective participation in social dialogue and policy advocacy. A key focus is on enabling EBMOs to contribute to the design, implementation, and monitoring of integrated policy frameworks that promote a conducive environment for sustainable enterprises, competitiveness, and productivity growth, including in the context of formalization and economic recovery. Through the Decent Work Country Programme for Zimbabwe, the ILO further supports EBMOs to actively engage in the Tripartite Negotiating Forum (TNF), including in the development and implementation of a national social contract and policy advocacy. At the same time, support is provided to enhance coordination and collaboration among EBMOs, enabling them to build a more unified and influential voice on key issues affecting the business community.
